articleSummary: Ocular toxoplasmosis in Misiones, Argentina, poses risks of retinal scarring and later reactivation. Ophthalmologist Nadia Flores notes that toxoplasmosis can be detected during routine fundus exams even in asymptomatic individuals. Misiones' subtropical climate favors the parasite's circulation; prevalence is high in Misiones, Corrientes, Santa Fe, and parts of Brazil. While cats can contribute to transmission, the parasite also resides in soil, contaminated vegetables, and undercooked meat; many exposures are asymptomatic but antibodies can be detected. In the eye, active lesions cause vision changes; the hallmark beacon in the fog includes red eye and blurred vision, with retinal lesions seen on fundoscopy. Treatment for active ocular disease may last about one month, with ongoing monitoring. Some scars never require meds, but reactivation risk remains. Prevention focuses on thoroughly cooking meat, cleaning produce, avoiding cross-contamination, hand hygiene, and ensuring veterinary care for pets, especially during pregnancy to prevent congenital toxoplasmosis.

articleHeadline: Targeted sequencing finds frequent TB and NTM co-detection in Chinese
articleSummary: In Jiangxi Province, southern China, a retrospective study of 83 Xpert MTB/RIF–positive respiratory specimens used targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) to re-examine for MTC and non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM). In bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, MTC and NTM co-occurred in 20 of 75 BAL samples (26.7%), representing 24.1% of patients. Among these 20 co-detected cases, three carried two additional NTM species alongside MTC, totaling 23 NTM detections: M. chelonae (12), M. abscessus (9), M. intracellulare (1), and M. gordonae (1). Genotypic fluoroquinolone resistance appeared in 9 of 83 patients (10.8%), with 14 gyrA mutations suggesting subclonal heteroresistance rather than confirmed phenotypic resistance. Mutations potentially for bedaquiline or clofazimine were unconfirmed. Two pre-XDR-TB cases were identified, both MDR with fluoroquinolone resistance. NAT2 acetylator genotypes ranged across slow, intermediate, and fast with no gender disparity. The integrated approach enables simultaneous pathogen detection, resistance profiling, and host pharmacogenetics, pending clinical validation and underscoring surveillance needs in Jiangxi.

articleSummary: Tuberculosis (TB) in smear-negative bronchoalveolar lavage fluid was assessed in a retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study at Hangzhou Red Cross Hospital, China, involving 6,560 patients (3,849 TB, 2,711 non-TB). Four tests—TB-DNA, SAT-TB, Xpert MTB/RIF, and mycobacterial culture—showed sensitivities of 48.4%, 38.0%, 52.1%, and 30.7%, with specificities of 99.6–100%. Xpert MTB/RIF demonstrated the highest single-test sensitivity and provided rifampicin-resistance data; among 1,002 Xpert plus phenotypic drug-susceptibility results, rifampicin resistance detection was 97.8% sensitive and 97.0% specific (kappa 0.841). Xpert plus TB-DNA yielded 61.4% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity. Adding SAT-TB and culture raised sensitivity to 64.9% (specificity 98.9%). Authors consider the additional gain modest and exploratory; they urge prospective studies on cost, turnaround time, and patient management before altering diagnostic algorithms. Limitations include retrospective, single-centre design and a composite reference standard in a five-year Chinese hospital population.

articleSummary: China: 2,253 children aged 1–14 hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia from October 2022 to June 2025 had at least one pathogen detected in 67.2% of cases. Across 2,324 pathogen-detection events, viral nucleic acids accounted for 45.1%, Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM positivity 43.8%, and bacterial culture 11.2%. Detected viruses with pneumonia relevance included human adenovirus, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus; Epstein-Barr virus was frequently codetected but not treated as a pneumonia-causing agent. Codetection occurred in 36.2% of pathogen-positive children (1,513 positive); within codetections, viral plus M. pneumoniae was predominant (69.3%). Severe community-acquired pneumonia was independently associated with viral detection, M. pneumoniae IgM positivity, codetection, and bacterial positivity. Findings support diagnostics tailored by age, region, and severity, and have implications for influenza and RSV prevention in post-pandemic China. Limitations: surveillance study and serology reflect immune response rather than direct pathogen ID.
